    <title>Scalable Edge Partitioning</title>
    <updated>2018-10-11T13:14:42Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.06411v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.06411v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Edge-centric distributed computations have appeared as a recent technique to improve the shortcomings of think-like-a-vertex algorithms on large scale-free networks. In order to increase parallelism on this model, edge partitioning - partitioning edges into roughly equally sized blocks - has emerged as an alternative to traditional (node-based) graph partitioning. In this work, we give a distributed memory parallel algorithm to compute high-quality edge partitions in a scalable way. Our algorithm scales to networks with billions of edges, and runs efficiently on thousands of PEs. Our technique is based on a fast parallelization of split graph construction and a use of advanced node partitioning algorithms.
